extracted.intended_audience: students and learners of Roman Catholic catechism (children and catechumens)
extracted.subtask_description: A question-and-answer instructional catechism covering the First through Fourth Commandments: definitions of sins (against faith, hope, charity), the honoring and invocation of saints, relics and images, and rules about oaths and vows. It gives doctrinal standards, moral obligations, examples, and anti-patterns for Catholic conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on sacramentals to excuse neglect of natural means
rubrics_metrics.description: Even with blessed sacramentals we must be careful not to go too far; it would be sinful willfully to expose ourselves to danger because we wear a scapular or expect miraculous protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A non-swimming boy must not plunge into deep water because he wears a scapular; a man who breaks his leg should seek medical treatment rather than 'look for miracles' when natural help will answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private revelations are not obligatory unless Church confirms them
rubrics_metrics.description: When holy people claim God revealed special things to them, we are not obliged to believe them unless the Church confirms it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some saints reported visions (e.g., St. Margaret Mary), the faithful must accept only what the Church authoritatively declares; believing unconfirmed private revelations is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject mediums, spiritists, and fortune-tellers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mediums and spiritists" are persons who pretend they can talk with the dead and whose work is deception and very sinful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All dealings with fortune-tellers etc. are giving to creatures what belongs to God alone; if such powers were real God would give them to the Church, not to a few sinful people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sins against faith are sins against the First Commandment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sins against faith occur by (1) not trying to know what God has taught; (2) refusing to believe what God has taught; (3) neglecting to profess belief in what God has taught.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and consequences: idling at Sunday school counts as 'not trying'; leaving the true religion is 'refusing to believe'; believing but not practicing (e.g., knowing to hear Mass but not going) is 'neglecting to profess' and gives scandal to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort required: try to know Christian doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to try to know what God has taught is committing a sin against faith by neglecting to learn the Christian doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend religious instruction, sermons, missions, and read good books; children who idle in catechism classes are cited as examples of this failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusing to believe: heretics and infidels defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who do not believe all that God has taught are heretics and infidels; categories include atheists, deists, infidels, heretics, apostates, and schismatics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and distinctions are given (e.g., atheist denies God's existence; deist denies revealed religion; heretics baptized but reject some doctrines; schismatics accept doctrines but reject papal authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting to profess belief is culpable
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who neglect to profess their belief in the true Church in which they believe fail to acknowledge the true Church and cannot expect salvation while in that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of excuses (upbringing, social consequences) are rejected; one must embrace the true religion when able, and may be obliged to make open profession when God's honor, neighbor's spiritual good, or personal good requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to make an open profession of faith
rubrics_metrics.description: We are obliged to make open profession of our faith as often as God's honor, our neighbor's spiritual good, or our own requires it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not need public proclamation at all times or to impudent questioners, but must act (e.g., refuse meat on Friday in a hotel, attend Mass publicly if others are indifferent) to promote God's honor and others' good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sins against hope: presumption and despair
rubrics_metrics.description: The sins against hope are presumption (rash expectation of salvation without proper means) and despair (loss of hope in God's mercy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both are grave: presumption includes living in deliberate sin expecting last-minute repentance; despair denies God's infinite mercy (Judas as example). Always maintain hope and seek confession/penance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption defined and cautioned against
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumption is a rash expectation of salvation without making proper use of the necessary means to obtain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: delaying repentance, repeatedly committing sins assuming confession later will absolve; resist temptation immediately and go to confession as soon as possible after mortal sin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Despair defined and opposed
rubrics_metrics.description: Despair is the loss of hope in God's mercy and is sinful because it denies God's infinite mercy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even grave sinners should hope for forgiveness—examples: Christ pardoned the thief on the cross and Mary Magdalene; one should call upon saints and ask others to pray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sins against love: all sin, especially mortal sin
rubrics_metrics.description: We sin against the love of God by all sin, but particularly by mortal sin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mortal sins sever charity and are the gravest offenses against the love of God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honoring and invoking saints is permitted and laudable
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Commandment does not forbid honoring the saints; by honoring saints we honor God Himself and may ask their intercession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invocation (asking saints to intercede) shows belief in God's majesty and our dependence; saints act as friends who can intercede before God on our behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praying to saints is asking for intercession, not worship
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not pray to the saints as to God; we ask them to 'obtain' favors for us, not to 'give' as God gives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liturgical language uses petitions like 'pray for us' rather than 'have mercy on us'; veneration differs from adoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: The communion of saints: definition and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The communion of saints is the union between members of the Church on earth, the blessed in Heaven, and souls in Purgatory; benefits include mutual assistance by prayers and good works and intercession by saints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains spiritual solidarity: faithful on earth assist and are aided by saints, while both help souls in Purgatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relics may be honored but must be authenticated
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Commandment does not forbid honoring relics (bodies or objects connected with saints or Our Lord), but relics must be examined and authenticated at Rome and accompanied by testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using anything as a relic without certainty of genuineness would be superstitious; Church-appointed examiners and marks/testimony are required for authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images permitted provided they are not adored as gods
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Commandment forbids making images to be adored as gods but does not forbid making images to put us in mind of Christ, His Mother, and the saints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogies (statues of Washington) show veneration of images as representation; images educate the ignorant and enliven devotion when treated as memorials, not objects of worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for images and relics, but do not pray to them as living
rubrics_metrics.description: It is right to show respect to pictures and images as representations; it is not allowed to pray to the crucifix or images and relics since they have no life or power to hear us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We pray before them because they enliven devotion and remind us of virtues to imitate; improper treatment of images dishonors what they represent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Commandment: reverence in speech and keeping oaths/vows
rubrics_metrics.description: The Second Commandment ('Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain') commands speaking with reverence of God, the saints, and holy things, and to keep lawful oaths and vows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using Scripture phrases in worldly ways is forbidden; the Church forbids using holy words for profane meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath: definition and when it is permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath is calling upon God to witness the truth of what we say; we may take an oath when ordered by lawful authority or required for God's honor or for our own or our neighbor's good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common lawful contexts: court testimony, officers taking office; the judge may require an oath to elicit truth in judicial matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for a lawful oath
rubrics_metrics.description: To make an oath lawful it is necessary that what we swear be true and that there be a sufficient cause for taking an oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rash oaths (swearing without certainty) and false oaths (perjury is vile); only swear when truth and sufficient reason support it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vow: definition, validity conditions, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A vow is a deliberate promise made to God to do something pleasing to Him; it must be made with full consent and freedom, to God, and to something lawful and pleasing to God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalid or sinful vows (e.g., promising to kill) are not true vows and should not be kept; vows made under coercion are not valid. Example: Herod's rash vow led to murder and was not binding because it was not proper to vow that which displeases God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbidden secret societies and obligations regarding vows/associations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church forbids joining secret societies whose objects are unlawful, whose means used are sinful, or which violate conscience by rash or dangerous oaths; legitimate associations for lawful ends (e.g., labor unions) are not forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership that exposes one to being forced to sin or to subvert Church authority is sinful; evaluate societies by their ends, means, and demands on conscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to fulfill lawful vows is sinful
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to fulfill our lawful vows is a sin, mortal or venial according to the nature of the vow and the intention with which it was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the seriousness of the vow and original intention when assessing culpability for breaking it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second Commandment forbids false, rash, unjust, unnecessary oaths and blasphemy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Second Commandment forbids all false, rash, unjust, and unnecessary oaths, blasphemy, cursing, and profane words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies 'rash' (swearing without knowing), defines 'blasphemy' (saying or doing something disrespectful to God, e.g., calling God unjust), and warns against actions or signs that defy God.
